Keyed `deployment` rather than `role`, which is reserved for the structural role each GROUP carries" data-fabric-ports="the thirteen 400G QSFP-DD ports are FABRIC ports and are for connecting to the fabric ports of an S9705-48D fabric switch only, not for service traffic (HIG Port Overview)" data-breakout="service ports 0-19 can individually break out into 4x25GE or 4x10GE; if any of ports 0-19 is in breakout mode the corresponding lower-column port is disabled (HIG Port Overview). Ports 20-39 are 40GE/100GE only" data-routing="full Segment Routing over IPv6 (SRv6) support (datasheet Key Features)" data-optics-qsfp28="100GE QSFP28 SR4, LR4, ER4 and ZR4, up to 80 km (datasheet Compatible Transceiver Types)" data-optics-sfp-plus="NOT STATED. The datasheet's Compatible Transceiver Types block lists 100GE QSFP28 SR4/LR4/ER4/ZR4 only and its Compatible Fabric Cable Types block lists 400GE QSFP-DD DAC/AEC/AOC; neither names anything for the two 10G SFP+ management ports, and the HIG's Connecting the Transceiver section names no part either. The cage takes what an SFP+ cage takes; which optics UfiSpace qualifies in it is unrecorded here rather than inferred - see the sfp-plus-optics gap" data-optics-qsfp-dd="400GE QSFP-DD DAC, AEC and AOC up to 100 m - the fabric ports take cables, and the datasheet's Compatible Fabric Cable Types list carries no optical transceiver" data-console="RJ45 RS-232 plus a micro-USB serial console, both lettered IOIOI" data-oob="1x RJ45 100/1000M out-of-band" data-inband-mgmt="2x 10G SFP+ management ports numbered 0 and 1" data-service-port="1x USB 2.0 Type-A" data-safety="UL 62368-1; IEC 62368-1; BSMI; NOM" data-emc="FCC Part 15, Subpart B, Class A; ICES-003, Class A; EN 55032, Class A; EN 55024; EN 55035; EN 62479; EN 50663; EN 300 386; EN 301 489; EN 303 413; BSMI; VCCI CISPR 32, Class A; AS/NZS CISPR 32, Class A; Anatel; NEBS GR-1089" data-environment="RoHS; WEEE; NEBS GR-63" data-nebs="the Regulatory Compliance table lists NEBS GR-1089 under EMC and NEBS GR-63 under Environment; separately the datasheet's Key Benefits line reads 'Ideal for Core, Edge, and Central Office deployments (NEBS Level 3)'. Both wordings are carried because they are different claims and neither document reconciles them" data-eol="none-announced" data-power="dc">
  <style>
    [data-path] { cursor: pointer; }
    .state-on    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-up    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    /* link and up are the same fact on an Ethernet lamp; see docs/rj45-family-design.md */
    .state-link  { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-activity { --led-color: #86efac; }
    .state-ok    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-fault { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-fail  { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-locate { --led-color: #3b82f6; }
    .state-absent { opacity: 0.35; }
    /* A SWITCHED OUTLET WITH NO LAMP is dimmed when it is off, as absent is but
       less (docs/pdu-model-design.md section 3.2): every switched PDU in the
       library has a lamp per outlet, and this is the fallback so the first one
       without does not invent a lamp. An outlet a lamp is bound to by `for:`
       carries data-lamped (mark_lamped) and is never dimmed: its lamp says it. */
    [data-class='inlet'][data-states~='off'].state-off:not([data-lamped]) { opacity: 0.55; }
    /* A state is a colour AND a behaviour. Solid and blinking of the same colour
       are different facts on real hardware: on the S9510-28DC a solid green PWR
       is "system power good" and a blinking green PWR is "power good but BMC
       power fail". A blinking state that renders solid is the same failure as a
       state class nothing paints - it looks modelled and is not.
       blink animates opacity rather than fill, because each skin carries its own
       unlit colour in the fill fallback and a keyframe cannot name it. alternate
       animates fill, because two colours is the whole point, and takes its first
       value from the element's own fill. */
    @keyframes portrayal-blink {
      0%, 49.9% { opacity: 1; }
      50%, 100% { opacity: 0; }
    }
    @keyframes portrayal-alternate {
      0%, 49.9% { fill: var(--led-color, #3a3f44); }
      50%, 100% { fill: var(--led-color-alt, #3a3f44); }
    }
    .portrayal-highlight { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.2px #f59e0b) drop-shadow(0 0 0.5px #f59e0b); }
    .portrayal-dim { opacity: 0.25; }
    [data-class='region'].portrayal-highlight { stroke: #f59e0b; stroke-width: 0.7; filter: none; }
    .state-fail[data-class='psu'], .state-fail[data-class='fan'] { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.4px #ef4444); }
</style>

<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="762mm" height="87.7mm" viewBox="0 0 762 87.7" data-device="s9700-53dx" data-view="right" data-switching-capacity="4.8 Tbps" data-packet-buffer="8 GB" data-power-typical-w="563" data-power-max-w="1434" data-power-envelope="bare" data-input-ac="200 to 240 V, 12.5 A" data-input-dc="-40 to -72 V, 60 A" data-psu-redundancy="1+1 hot-swappable, active-active" data-fan-redundancy="3+1 hot-swappable" data-airflow="front-to-back" data-operating-temp="0 to 45 C" data-operating-humidity="5 to 85% RH non-condensing" data-storage-temp="-40 to 70 C" data-storage-humidity="5 to 93% RH non-condensing" data-asic="Broadcom Jericho2 BCM88690" data-tcam="Broadcom OP2 BCM16K external TCAM for additional table sizes" data-cpu="Intel Broadwell-DE 8-core @ 2.0 GHz" data-memory="64 GB DDR4" data-storage="128 GB SSD" data-bmc="Aspeed AST2400" data-deployment="functions standalone or as a node in a cluster from 4 Tbps up to 192 Tbps; interoperable with the rest of the S9700 series using an S9705-48D or S9725-64E as the fabric (datasheet Key Features). Keyed `deployment` rather than `role`, which is reserved for the structural role each GROUP carries" data-fabric-ports="the thirteen 400G QSFP-DD ports are FABRIC ports and are for connecting to the fabric ports of an S9705-48D fabric switch only, not for service traffic (HIG Port Overview)" data-breakout="service ports 0-19 can individually break out into 4x25GE or 4x10GE; if any of ports 0-19 is in breakout mode the corresponding lower-column port is disabled (HIG Port Overview). Ports 20-39 are 40GE/100GE only" data-routing="full Segment Routing over IPv6 (SRv6) support (datasheet Key Features)" data-optics-qsfp28="100GE QSFP28 SR4, LR4, ER4 and ZR4, up to 80 km (datasheet Compatible Transceiver Types)" data-optics-sfp-plus="NOT STATED. The datasheet's Compatible Transceiver Types block lists 100GE QSFP28 SR4/LR4/ER4/ZR4 only and its Compatible Fabric Cable Types block lists 400GE QSFP-DD DAC/AEC/AOC; neither names anything for the two 10G SFP+ management ports, and the HIG's Connecting the Transceiver section names no part either. The cage takes what an SFP+ cage takes; which optics UfiSpace qualifies in it is unrecorded here rather than inferred - see the sfp-plus-optics gap" data-optics-qsfp-dd="400GE QSFP-DD DAC, AEC and AOC up to 100 m - the fabric ports take cables, and the datasheet's Compatible Fabric Cable Types list carries no optical transceiver" data-console="RJ45 RS-232 plus a micro-USB serial console, both lettered IOIOI" data-oob="1x RJ45 100/1000M out-of-band" data-inband-mgmt="2x 10G SFP+ management ports numbered 0 and 1" data-service-port="1x USB 2.0 Type-A" data-safety="UL 62368-1; IEC 62368-1; BSMI; NOM" data-emc="FCC Part 15, Subpart B, Class A; ICES-003, Class A; EN 55032, Class A; EN 55024; EN 55035; EN 62479; EN 50663; EN 300 386; EN 301 489; EN 303 413; BSMI; VCCI CISPR 32, Class A; AS/NZS CISPR 32, Class A; Anatel; NEBS GR-1089" data-environment="RoHS; WEEE; NEBS GR-63" data-nebs="the Regulatory Compliance table lists NEBS GR-1089 under EMC and NEBS GR-63 under Environment; separately the datasheet's Key Benefits line reads 'Ideal for Core, Edge, and Central Office deployments (NEBS Level 3)'. Both wordings are carried because they are different claims and neither document reconciles them" data-eol="none-announced" data-power="dc">
  <style>
    [data-path] { cursor: pointer; }
    .state-on    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-up    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    /* link and up are the same fact on an Ethernet lamp; see docs/rj45-family-design.md */
    .state-link  { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-activity { --led-color: #86efac; }
    .state-ok    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-fault { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-fail  { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-locate { --led-color: #3b82f6; }
    .state-absent { opacity: 0.35; }
    /* A SWITCHED OUTLET WITH NO LAMP is dimmed when it is off, as absent is but
       less (docs/pdu-model-design.md section 3.2): every switched PDU in the
       library has a lamp per outlet, and this is the fallback so the first one
       without does not invent a lamp. An outlet a lamp is bound to by `for:`
       carries data-lamped (mark_lamped) and is never dimmed: its lamp says it. */
    [data-class='inlet'][data-states~='off'].state-off:not([data-lamped]) { opacity: 0.55; }
